findings.description: ACQUISITION/ENCODING CONTRACT IS ENTIRELY ABSENT FROM THE SPEC. The EARS says only *which source* the stamp comes from (GOOGLEFINANCE's quote date, not wall clock). It says nothing about how that date is obtained or encoded. The code pins a large, exact mechanism: a companion `Quote Date` column published as the last column (M) of `POSITIONS_HEADER` (lib.rs:187, 590), rendered as a live `Cell::Formula` with the exact text `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("TICKER","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` (`quote_date_formula`, lib.rs:270-274) — i.e. the `tradetime` attribute (not `datadate`/`date`), `INT()` truncation to a date serial, re-basing to the kernel epoch by subtracting `DATE(1970,1,1)`, and `TEXT(...,"0")` digits-only rendering so the values-API read-back is locale-independent. None of that is in the spec text. Symmetrically, all three A-runs were forced to invent the mechanism and invented it three different ways, all of them wrong relative to the real design: A1 and A3 wrote an in-crate parser over a Sheets serial with a **1899-12-30** epoch plus ISO `%Y-%m-%d` and US `%m/%d/%Y` text fallbacks; A2 pushed parsing upstream. The real code does the normalization *in the sheet* and does no parsing in `sheets-view` at all. This one silence in the spec is what both directions are pointing at.

CARRY-FORWARD PRESERVES THE OLD STAMP — NEVER RE-STAMPS. The spec's 'stamp each cached mark' is silent on what happens to a symbol that does not settle this pass. The code pins it hard: in `read_marks`, `Some(PriceReading::Transient) | None` with a `prior` entry does `out.marks.insert(s.clone(), *prev)` (lib.rs:873-879) — the whole prior `Mark` including its original `quote_date`, so a carried mark keeps a stale quote epoch and is NOT recorded degraded. `transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window` (tests/marks.rs:162-191) asserts equality against `Mark { Cents(180_00), Date(19_100) }`, and `Mark` is `Copy`/`Eq` so that equality includes the stamp. All three B-runs recovered this as a first-class rule; no A-run has any notion of carry-forward, because the spec sentence gives no hook for one. The spec also never states the resulting property that downstream consumers depend on — a mark's stamp reveals its true age rather than the age of the pass that emitted it.

THE NO-FALLBACK GUARANTEE THE SPEC FORCES IS UNPINNED AT THE SEAM. 'not the wall-clock read time' is a prohibition, and all three A-runs read it the same way: a missing/blank/unparsable quote date must be a hard reject (`MarkError::MissingQuoteDate` / `MarkReject::NoQuoteDate`), explicitly reasoning that a silent wall-clock fallback would violate the very requirement. The real code has no such path and cannot express the case: `PriceReading::Numeric { price_usd, quote_date: Date }` structurally *requires* a date, so 'price settled but quote date blank' is inexpressible in `sheets-view`, and there is no `DegradeReason` variant for it (`TimedOut` / `Permanent` / `SubCent` only, lib.rs:301-311). This is not hypothetical: the code's own formula emits `""` via `IFERROR` whenever `tradetime` is loading or errored, and `price` and `tradetime` are separate GOOGLEFINANCE attributes that can disagree (price resolves, `tradetime` unsupported/errored for some instruments). Whichever out-of-crate client implements `read_price_pass` therefore decides — untested and unconstrained — whether that empty cell becomes `Transient`, `Permanent`, or a fabricated date. No test in tests/marks.rs covers an empty Quote Date cell alongside a numeric price.

DEGRADATION GATES THE STAMP, WITH CONSTANTS THE SPEC NEVER MENTIONS. The code pins exactly which symbols get no stamp at all: `price_to_cents` returns `Err(DegradeReason::Permanent)` for non-finite and `Err(DegradeReason::SubCent)` for any result `cents <= 0` (lib.rs:362-385) — so a positive sub-cent price, an exact `0.0`, and a negative price all yield no mark and therefore no quote-date stamp regardless of the reading's `quote_date`; a `Permanent` reading degrades with *no* prior carry (unlike `Transient`, lib.rs:881-883); a `Transient` symbol past the window with no prior degrades `TimedOut`. Boundary constants pinned by code+tests but absent from the spec: `SettleConfig::default().max_polls = 8` (lib.rs:788) and `DATA_START_ROW = 2`. All three B-runs recovered this cluster; the spec sentence implies none of it.

THE STAMP IS PRODUCED BUT NEVER CONSUMED BY THE KERNEL. `to_ledger_marks()` maps `(s, m) -> (s.clone(), m.price_cents)` (lib.rs:341-346), dropping `quote_date` entirely — the stamp lives only in `MarksProduced.marks` for `runtime`'s cache and never crosses into replay. The spec says to stamp each cached mark but never states that the stamp is view/cache-layer provenance with no path into the accounting kernel, nor that a degraded symbol is simply *absent* from the ledger marks map (pinned by `degraded_symbol_absent_from_ledger_marks_for_per_symbol_degradation`, tests/marks.rs:267-313). Two of three B-runs called this out explicitly.

MARK SHAPE AND EPOCH ARE CODE-SIDE ONLY. The spec states a negative ('not the wall-clock read time') but never the positive: that a `Mark` is exactly `(price_cents: Cents, quote_date: Date)` with no read-time, publish-time, or ingestion-time field anywhere in the struct; that `Date` is days since 1970-01-01 (the kernel epoch the sheet formula re-bases to); and that `Mark` derives `Copy`/`PartialEq`/`Eq` so mark equality includes the stamp. B1 and B2 both promoted 'there is no wall-clock field on a mark' to a ubiquitous requirement — a structural guarantee the code delivers (no clock parameter reaches `read_marks` at all, matching all three A-runs' 'takes no clock' reasoning) but that the spec text never states as a shape constraint.

TRANSPORT-FAILURE BOUNDARY. On `read_price_pass` error, `read_marks` propagates `Err(ViewError)` and produces no `MarksProduced` — it does not emit an empty marks set and does not itself carry `prior` (stamped) marks forward; offline carry-forward of stamped marks is explicitly `runtime`'s responsibility (lib.rs:806-828, test `transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks`). All three B-runs surfaced this as a stamping-adjacent rule ('no stamps are fabricated'); the spec text has no boundary/ownership clause at all.

notes:
A-side agreement is high on interpretation and semantics: all three read 'stamp' as the mark's as-of/provenance field, all three deliberately omit any clock parameter as the structural guarantee, all three use date granularity (NaiveDate/Date, no time-of-day), all three hard-reject a missing/unparsable date rather than falling back, and all three declare staleness policy and timezone normalization out of scope. They diverge only on where parsing lives (A1/A3 inline, A2 upstream) — which is itself evidence for finding 1, not instability.

B-side agreement is near-verbatim: all three recovered the exact formula string, column M as the last POSITIONS_HEADER entry, the 1970-01-01 epoch and the INT/-DATE/TEXT rationale, `IFERROR -> ""` on loading/error, verbatim quote_date carry on Numeric, unchanged prior-mark carry-forward including the stamp, degraded-symbols-get-no-stamp, absence from `to_ledger_marks()`, Err propagation with runtime owning offline carry, and `max_polls = 8`.

False positives deliberately excluded. (1) A-side 'no clock parameter' is NOT drift — the real code has no clock in scope anywhere in the mark path, so both sides agree. (2) A-side 'companion quote-date column exists' is NOT drift — the code has exactly that (column M), even though the spec never says so; the spec-silence is already captured in finding 1. (3) A2's 'missing price also rejects' is an assumption artifact (A2 flags it itself as beyond the EARS). (4) The 1899-12-30 Sheets serial epoch and the ISO/US text formats are inventions with no spec basis; I fold them in as evidence of underspecification rather than claiming them as standalone findings.

The core assertion of the spec IS honored and directly tested (`mark_stamped_with_googlefinance_quote_date_not_wall_clock`, tests/marks.rs:244-264, pinning Date(19_100) surviving into the mark). The drift is not a violation of the sentence — it is that the sentence is one clause covering a contract with roughly a dozen load-bearing decisions in it.
